name: personal-finance
description: The monthly close of a household ledger: the second workload definition, and the worked example's. Unit types are the steps of a close; each names the profile it runs under and the checks the host runs on its output — the ledger's own test suite, run by the orchestrator, is the reconciliation. Nothing here moves money: a payment is a file a person executes, written only after consent.

unitTypes.name: ingest
unitTypes.description: Copy one period's statement rows into the ledger, every row in the holding category. The statement is the bank's and is never edited.

unitTypes.name: categorize
unitTypes.description: Assign each ledger row a category from the taxonomy. A merchant the statement does not explain stays in the holding category and is surfaced, never guessed.

unitTypes.name: reconcile
unitTypes.description: Read the period's ledger against its statement and say what does not match. Read-only: it reports, and the host's run of the ledger's checks is the evidence.

unitTypes.name: report
unitTypes.description: Write the period's close under reports/: totals by category and open items. The totals are checked against the ledger by the host, not taken from the report.

unitTypes.name: prepare-payment
unitTypes.description: Write a payment the household will make under payments/pending/, after consent from a person. Writing the file is the commitment; the transfer itself is the person's.

unitTypes.name: close
unitTypes.description: Confirm the period's evidence is fresh and its open items are dispositioned. Read-only.
